_doc: Config for scripts/polisade_drift_gate.py — deterministic arch<->code drift gate (blocking in CI). Full field reference: docs/config-reference.md in the Polisade Orchestrator repo. JSON has no comments, so `_doc` keys carry them; the gate ignores every key starting with `_`.

api._doc: OpenAPI paths+methods declared in design artifacts vs route declarations in code. Built-in extractors: fastapi/flask, express, nestjs, spring; `auto` runs them all. For anything else use custom_route_regex with named groups (?P<method>...) and (?P<path>...).

er._doc: Mermaid erDiagram entities/attributes in design artifacts vs the DB schema. Built-in extractors: sql-ddl, sqlalchemy, prisma; `auto` runs them all. naming.map pins entity->table names the heuristics cannot guess.
er._doc_types: Since issue #85 a column carries type / length / nullable / default, and a field is compared ONLY when both sides declare it (absence is never drift). Type spelling is normalised through one cross-language table inside the script; type_map overrides and extends it (lowercase raw spelling -> canonical name), e.g. {"inn_t": "VARCHAR"}. There is no per-stack preset. SQL DDL, Prisma and SQLAlchemy that describe one column differently give er.schema_conflict — that is the ORM-vs-migration case. Mermaid has no nullability syntax: the ER side reads it only from an attribute comment whose comma-separated position is exactly `not null` / `nullable` / `null` / `required` / `optional`, plus PK. Mermaid has no DEFAULT syntax either, so fail_on_default_mismatch reaches only the schema<->schema half; it gates both halves so it cannot be bypassed. missing_column needs a COMPLETE extractor (a CREATE TABLE body or a Prisma model): an ALTER-only migration directory is an increment, not a table. timestamptz and timestamp without time zone normalise DIFFERENTLY on purpose (as do TIMESTAMP(6) WITH TIME ZONE and DateTime(timezone=True)) - collapse them via type_map if the project does not care. The three per-field switches gate BOTH halves symmetrically: fail_on_type_mismatch=false also silences a type disagreement reported as er.schema_conflict.
